:::{#thm-bsc-capacity}
#### Capacity of the binary symmetric channel

The [binary symmetric channel](#def-binary-symmetric-channel)
with crossover [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $\epsilon$
has [capacity](channel-capacity.qmd#def-channel-capacity)

$$C = 1 - h(\epsilon) \text{ bits per channel use},$$

where $h$ is the [binary entropy function](#def-binary-entropy).
A uniform [input](#def-channel) achieves it.

:::

::: {.proof}

Fix any [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) for $X$.
By [mutual information as a reduction in entropy](entropy.qmd#thm-mutual-information-reduction),

$$\mutinfof{X}{Y} = \entropyf{Y} - \entropyf{Y \mid X}.$$

Given $X = x$, the output equals $x$ with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1 - \epsilon$
and differs from it with probability $\epsilon$,
so the [entropy of $Y$ given $X = x$](entropy.qmd#def-entropy-given-value)
is $h(\epsilon)$ for both values of $x$.
Averaging over $x$, the [conditional entropy](entropy.qmd#def-conditional-entropy)
is $\entropyf{Y \mid X} = h(\epsilon)$, whatever $X$ is.

$Y$ takes two values, so $\entropyf{Y} \le \log_2 2 = 1$ [bit](entropy.qmd#def-bit)
[@cover2006elements, section 2.6].
Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mutinfof{X}{Y}
&= \entropyf{Y} - h(\epsilon) \\
&\le 1 - h(\epsilon).
\end{aligned}
$$

If $X$ is uniform on $\{0, 1\}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\P(Y = 1)
&= \P(X = 0) \, \epsilon + \P(X = 1) \, (1 - \epsilon) \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \epsilon + \tfrac{1}{2} (1 - \epsilon) \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2},
\end{aligned}
$$

so $\entropyf{Y} = 1$ bit and $\mutinfof{X}{Y} = 1 - h(\epsilon)$.
This value is attained, so it is the [maximum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-maximum) $C$.

:::
